---
title: "cancel-superseded.yml"
---

Cancels the queued and running workflow runs of a pull request
that were started for a head the pull request no longer has,
and, once the pull request closes, the runs started before it closed.
This implements
[gha#1400](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/issues/1400).

Runs started at or after the close are left alone,
so a `closed` workflow such as preview teardown still runs.

## Inputs

| Input | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `runs-on` | `vars.CI_RUNNER` in a private repository that sets it; otherwise `ubuntu-latest` | Runner label for the job |

## Permissions

The caller grants `actions: write` and `pull-requests: read`.

## Limits

- GitHub lists no pull request for a run from a fork,
  so fork pull requests are never matched.
- Runs in `waiting` or `requested` status are not cancelled.
- Fork and Dependabot pull requests get a read-only token,
  which cannot cancel runs.
- GitHub runs no `pull_request` workflow while a pull request has merge conflicts,
  so the caller does not fire, and nothing is cancelled, until the conflict is resolved.
- On a self-hosted runner pool (`CI_RUNNER`), the cancel job queues for a runner
  like any other job, so it can wait behind the very runs it should cancel.
  Set `runs-on` to a label with a free runner if that delay matters.

## Example

See
[`examples/cancel-superseded.yml`](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/blob/main/examples/cancel-superseded.yml).
